The company that abolished the dual system of government in Bengal was the **British East India Company** (often referred to simply as the East India Company).

The dual system of government in Bengal, introduced by Robert Clive in 1765, gave the Company the right to collect revenue (Diwani) while the Nawab retained administrative and judicial powers (Nizamat). This system was abolished by **Warren Hastings** through the **Regulating Act of 1773**, which brought Bengal under direct British Crown control and ended the dual administration.

The East India Company itself was established by a Royal Charter granted by Queen Elizabeth I on **December 31, 1600**.

Exact Answer: 1600
